_comment: Controlled vocabulary for the topicId field on native question-bank items. One entry per physics topic, independent of any course's unit numbering. build/validate.js checks every bank item's topicId against this list and confirms the item's courses are a subset of the topic's declared courses. Prose rationale and the conversion workflow live in docs/question-bank-topics.md.

kinematics-1d.title: One-dimensional kinematics
kinematics-1d.scope: Motion language, position/velocity/acceleration-time graphs, constant-acceleration equations, 1-D free fall, vector components and SOHCAHTOA. No projectile motion, force-based reasoning, or calculus.

forces-and-newtons-laws.title: Forces and Newton's laws (introductory)
forces-and-newtons-laws.scope: Gravity (universal gravitation), inertia and Newton's first law, force identification and free-body diagrams, equilibrium, Newton's second law, inclined planes (with and without friction), Newton's third law, Hooke's law. 1-D net-force reasoning and simple inclines; no 2-D vector force addition beyond incline components. The pre-AP subset of `newtonian-dynamics`.

mechanical-energy.title: Mechanical energy (introductory)
mechanical-energy.scope: Work ($W = Fd$ for angles $0^\circ$, $90^\circ$, $180^\circ$), total and mechanical energy, gravitational potential energy ($mgh$), kinetic energy ($\tfrac12 mv^2$), conservation of mechanical energy in isolated systems, spring potential energy ($\tfrac12 kx^2$), and the work-energy theorem ($W_{net} = \Delta KE$). Scalar energy accounting; no 2-D work integrals or power.

newtonian-dynamics.title: Newtonian dynamics (AP Physics 1 Unit 2)
newtonian-dynamics.scope: Systems and centre of mass, force identification and free-body diagrams, Newton's three laws, static and kinetic friction, connected objects and pulleys, inclined planes with 2-D component resolution, gravitation / springs / apparent weight, and uniform circular motion. The full AP Physics 1 Unit 2 (Force and Translational Dynamics) scope; a superset of the pre-AP `forces-and-newtons-laws` topic.
